tasks.intent: Read and decode several files from one continuous charge in parallel
tasks.requires: Complete file list, DBC and signal bindings, established time coordinates and an explicit merge choice; positive worker limit.
tasks.check: The cross-file integral is 38 J. Configuration allows four workers, capped at two for the two files. The time-order extension has one event from 0 to 6 s, confirmed at 1 s.

references.description: Process limits, ordering, resource and error rules

tasks.intent: Rolling current or rate on CAN frames with irregular timestamps
tasks.requires: Current field and unit, valid_for, actual/fixed/DBC clock, driver, window and output step.
tasks.check: At 0.20 s the mean is 130/9 A with a 100 ms DBC period; actual time gives 18 A. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Register a trusted custom point function, sample reduction or stateful grid operation in Python
tasks.requires: The accompanying host program, ASC and DBC; a version, typed ports, supported backends and a budget contract.
tasks.check: The host reports 80 A peak and 10, 20, 30, 30 A for the valid grid outputs. Use the host script to supply the registry. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Integrate power from BLF / ASC messages
tasks.requires: Logs, channel, matching DBC, power unit, and clock.
tasks.check: Check joules (J) and the actual observed range. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Continuous BLF/ASC volumes: require multiple conditions for longer than a threshold, then integrate energy over the full qualifying interval in kWh
tasks.requires: Raw ASC/BLF and matching DBC; target signals, codes, units, comparisons, continuous duration, and integration scope. Do not require types, units, or periods to be repeated when the DBC supplies them.
tasks.applicable: Custom state and numeric conditions; inclusive or strict duration thresholds; integration from condition onset; optional energy unit. The example uses strict >60s, default onset, and actual elapsed time.
tasks.not_applicable: For per-message contributions query MESSAGE_ENERGY; choose FAST_MESSAGE_ENERGY only when its current-message restrictions fit. Independent tasks use BATCH; fast template totals use FAST_TEMPLATE_TOTAL.
tasks.alternative: charge_session applies only to its strict current > comparison, duration >= comparison, Wh/Ah outputs, and direction/measurement-point requirements. Do not choose it merely because a task mentions charging.
tasks.check: Exactly 60 seconds produces no event. The cross-file 61-second interval is [61,122), giving 4000W*61s/3600000=0.06777777777777777kWh. Link parent_id to event_id and check status/reason. Do not replace strict comparison with 60.1 seconds. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Power table integrated using actual elapsed time
tasks.requires: Time column, units, power column, and validity period.
tasks.check: Compare with the hand-calculated 38 J.

tasks.intent: Charging activities, electric charge, and charging energy
tasks.requires: Mode codes, positive current direction, terminal measurement point, voltage, thresholds, and duration. The teaching example uses ASC; for BLF replace the logs, DBC, and bindings with your own.
tasks.check: Check each activity boundary and Wh/Ah result. Current exactly equal to current_min is excluded; duration exactly equal to minimum_duration qualifies. The default start is onset. Check applicability rather than matching only the word charging. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.
tasks.applicable: Mode equals the specified integer code and current is strictly greater than current_min. After reaching minimum_duration, calculate from condition onset. Outputs are Wh for energy and Ah for electric charge. Positive current means charging, and the measurement point is the battery-pack terminal.
tasks.not_applicable: Do not directly apply charge_session when the task needs current >= threshold, a strict duration threshold, direct kWh output, another state combination, or unconfirmed preset direction/measurement-point requirements.
tasks.alternative: Use CONDITION_ENERGY and ../../Current/examples/conditional-energy.yaml with an ordinary condition_duration rule and event-scope integral. Preserve the comparisons, duration comparison, and output unit. Ordinary U*I integration needs no extra direction/measurement-point metadata or 95% coverage threshold.

tasks.intent: Sustained activities, exit grouping, and event relationships
tasks.requires: Condition, time units, window, and allowed gap.
tasks.check: Preserve event boundaries; a segment may contain multiple parent_event_ids. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Alarm context and rising edges
tasks.requires: An explicitly defined Boolean alarm and before/after durations.
tasks.check: Check point events separately from surrounding segments. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Request/response pairs, timeout, and insufficient observation
tasks.requires: Comparable request and response clocks, with explicit minimum and maximum delays.
tasks.check: Unknown observations must not become a definite no-response outcome. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Boolean and enumeration codes, and expression aliases
tasks.requires: Equipment code definitions; undefined codes must not use nonzero=true.
tasks.check: Expressions reference bound names. Semantic IDs are not attribute paths. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Conversions, units, and scales
tasks.requires: Input/target units and existing DBC conversion; establish direction only when the task needs that interpretation.
tasks.check: Infer conversion from declared input and target units when scale and offset are both omitted; 2000 mA becomes 2 A. DBC coefficients apply only once. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Expired data, zero values, and partial results
tasks.requires: Period or validity, required observation range, and missing-data policy.
tasks.check: Read status/reason/quality together with the value. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Run independent tasks in a batch
tasks.requires: Independent input and output for each plan, without shared task state.
tasks.check: Use batch run. The basic file sets root process_count to 4 (software default 1) and child plans to 1. Inspect worker_process_count and each worker_pid; one job uses at most one task worker. Keep continuous volumes in one task source.

tasks.intent: Shared definitions, field origins, and relative paths
tasks.requires: Both the main configuration and referenced shared-definition files.
tasks.check: Use config origins --fields to inspect declaration origins. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Export raw messages around events
tasks.requires: A supported CAN source, explicit window, and writable output directory; existing results may remain there.
tasks.check: Check actual windows, output format, and manifest. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Load, publish, and close results in Python
tasks.requires: The matching installed version, complete plan, and writable result directory; use the actual manifest path returned by write.
tasks.check: Run ../run_analysis.py. Validate before execution, read rows, and close resources.

tasks.intent: Correct configuration using diagnostics
tasks.requires: The user's original intent, original files, and actual diagnostics.
tasks.check: Fix field placement, types, or references. Do not remove conditions or change validity to suppress errors.

tasks.intent: Map ASC/DBC voltage through a calibration curve and calculate mean power
tasks.requires: Input unit, calibration points and output unit.
tasks.check: 3, 7 and 3 V give 10, 30 and 10 W; the mean is about 16.67 W. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Calculate sample and time-weighted power statistics, and aggregate scalar calculation rows, sequence delays, event counts or final segment counts
tasks.requires: Define the result population, named source, operation and grouping. Confirm whether partial values may participate and how an incomplete population is reported. The example uses P95 of per-event means; references cover calculation, sequence, rule and window sources.
tasks.check: Five readings, two starts, two loaded activities and one merged segment. P95 of readings is 18 W. P95 across load means is 19.5 W with two candidates and two included. Time RMS is about 11.05542 W. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.

tasks.intent: Accumulate each target CAN message contribution using the general analysis runner
tasks.requires: Confirm the target channel/frame, DBC, units and the contribution computed by expr. Confirm a time factor when converting power to energy; it is unnecessary for contributions already expressed as energy. Read references for all fields and restrictions.
tasks.check: Two simultaneous 4000 W messages each contribute 400 J at 0.1 s, totaling 800 J; the record at 1 s is outside [0,1). The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.
tasks.applicable: Use general run for CAN per-message accumulation, including continuous source files or requested contribution details. Values come from the current target message.
tasks.not_applicable: Not elapsed-time integration or cross-message cached values. For one ASC/BLF source with all inputs in the target frame, compare FAST_MESSAGE_ENERGY and its restrictions.

tasks.intent: Accumulate energy per matched CAN message in one ASC or BLF
tasks.requires: Confirm the unit, contribution time, frame ID, DBC, channel and sign bucket.
tasks.check: Open the manifest at this run manifest_path, then its CSV. Two simultaneous 400 J contributions give 800 J. No target frames gives null; valid target frames with an empty direction bucket give zero. Read status/reason with the value. The example sets execution.process_count to 4; the number of input files caps actual workers, so a single file uses at most one.
tasks.applicable: One ASC/BLF source with all formula inputs in the current frame; see FAST_CONTINUOUS_SESSION for multiple volumes.
tasks.not_applicable: No cross-message holding, events/windows, elapsed-time integration, raw CSV or multiplex/container frames.

tasks.intent: Compute per-metric totals across independent files from one template
tasks.requires: Confirm independent runs and the same template. Select only the intended inputs.
tasks.check: Open report_path. The inputs yield 800 and 400 J, giving a complete 1200 J total. Totals require explicit --total. Check every member per metric; do not replace missing values with zero.

tasks.intent: Compute one recording across ASC/BLF volumes with multiple workers and one session summary
tasks.requires: Confirm one source and current-message contributions; choose file_merge deliberately and set the worker count.
tasks.check: Three 400 J contributions total 1200 J. Configuration allows four workers; the two input files use two. Check statuses and counts rather than applying independent-batch missing-value rules.
